messages:
sam: CI red on linux worker-7 for `serve/tests/test_backpressure.py::test_retry_on_backpressure`. Failed 2x in the last 6 runs. Can't reproduce locally.

matt: Got a link to the failing build? Can you paste the tail of the log?

sam: https://ci.buildkite.com/teams/redwood/builds/98765#job-7 — failing log: 
```
E       AssertionError: expected 3 retries, got 2
serve/retry.py:142: AssertionError
[INFO] backpressure: queued=12 inflight=4
[DEBUG] retry: scheduling retry after 120ms
```
Happens right after a burst of synthetic load in the test harness.

ci-bot: @sam triggered rerun (build 98765) — rerun job 98765.2 queued :repeat:

elaine: Can you run this locally with `TEST_REPEAT=200` and `PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-k retry_on_backpressure -q'`? If it's timing-sensitive, increasing repeat helps. Also try `--capture=no` so we can see interleaved logs.

sam: Running `TEST_REPEAT=200 pytest serve/tests/test_backpressure.py::test_retry_on_backpressure --maxfail=1 -q --capture=no` now. If it doesn't reproduce, we should try docker parity with the CI runner.

kevin: I can run the bisect tomorrow. Range? last green was `main@9f2c1d` and failures started `main@9f2c1f` according to the flaky history. I usually do `git bisect run ./scripts/bisect_test.sh serve/tests/test_backpressure.py::test_retry_on_backpressure` with the test wrapper that sets stable seeds.

lisa: FYI, test harness changed two weeks ago to use the new async executor shim — could be a scheduling/timing delta. Might be worth adding a short sleep in the test to see if it's strictly a race.

sam: Local repeat 200: 0 reproductions so far (30m). Docker local with `--cpus=2 --memory=4g` and the same kernel settings also 0/100. CI shows it fails only on worker-7 (seems nondeterministic and hardware-related?).

matt: Can you try forcing the same kernel scheduler flags as the CI worker? e.g., `sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=5000000` — not ideal but a useful check.

sam: Tried kernel tweak; still no repro. CI rerun result: build 98765.2 = failed (same assertion). logs: 
```
E       AssertionError: expected 3 retries, got 2
serve/retry.py:142
[DEBUG] kvcache: evicting prefix id=0x1b
[DEBUG] backpressure: drained=1, woke=0
```

ci-bot: Rerun queued by @sam completed: 1/2 failures across recent tries. See flaky-history dashboard for counts.

elaine: Let's avoid blocking landing. Plan: (1) add flaky label to the test and a temporary rerun step in CI (run twice), (2) schedule kevin to bisect, (3) add extra logging (show timing and scheduler info) on failure.

kevin: I'll take the bisect. Will run `git bisect` with the bisect script and include `--repeat=20` per candidate since it's intermittent. If bisect narrows to a commit that touched the async executor or retry backoff, we open a revert or targeted fix.

matt: Also drop a small debug patch onto main that logs `TEST_SEED`, `THREAD_COUNT`, and `kernel.sched_*` at test start. If the failure surfaces again in CI we get more signal without rerunning manually.

sam: I pushed `debug/retry-flake-logging` with a tiny change to print env and scheduler info on failure. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3145. Added `--max-retries=3` assertion to be explicit and a better error message.

lisa: Thanks — that will help. If bisect converges to something non-obvious, we might try isolating the test into a dedicated runner with identical container image as worker-7.

kevin: Starting bisect now. Will post progress here every few hours. Initial comment: out of the first 40 candidates, 3 were inconclusive; setting `--repeat=50` for those.

sam: Appreciated. Adding `needs-bisect` label to the flaky board. Also I'll schedule a periodic CI job to run this test 1000x on a canary runner overnight to collect failure traces.

matt: Quick note — avoid force-reverting anything without confirmation. This looks timing/nondeterministic; a revert might not help if the root cause is environmental.

ci-bot: build 98765.3 (manual rerun) completed: passed. Current rolling stats: 4 passes / 3 fails in last 12 runs.

elaine: OK still flaky. kevin, ping here when bisect finds a suspect commit. If nothing in 24h, we'll escalate to runtime-owners and consider an aggressive mitigation (short sleep or bumping backoff gap) behind a feature flag.

kevin: Will do. First suspicious commit touches `executor/shim.rs` and `serve/retry.py` — running extra repeats on that candidate now.

sam: Thanks team. I'll keep the rerun step and flaky label until we have a root cause. :thumbsup:
